chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` truncates the stop reason to `cfg.lanes.fleet_reason_chars` before that reason is used by `_class` for failed-pattern matching, so a display cap can change an agent’s class. For example, with `cfg.lanes.fleet_reason_chars = 5`, `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`, and a `lease.expired` event whose reason is `"HTTP 429"`, `_signals` stores only `LN.safe("HTTP 429")[:5]`, i.e. `"HTTP "`. `_class` then searches `"429"` against `"HTTP "` and returns `STALLED`, so `registry` lists the stopped lane as stalled instead of failed. If `fleet_reason_chars` is `0`, the stored reason is empty and rate-limit/failed patterns cannot match at all. The reason length cap should affect display, not the classification of failed vs stalled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:_signals

chunk_findings.detail: The new `resume` operation has two contradictory target contracts. The `view` help says `resume` is “the one idempotent resume for lane” and the positional parameter that carries it is declared as `lane` (“Lane name (or a unique part); with view=brief or resume”), while the CLI help and docs say `ddflow lanes resume <agent>` and the call only forwards that second positional as `lane=a.get("lane")`. Thus `ddflow lanes resume worker-1` (agent name per docs) and `ddflow lanes resume feature-x` (lane name per the `view`/`lane` help) cannot both be correct; one documented input will fail to identify the intended fleet entry or will target the wrong lane/agent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lanes.py:38/45 and docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/fleet-registry.md:8

chunk_findings.detail: This test is supposed to verify that a long, backtick-containing session summary is truncated and sanitized, but its only assertions are `len(r) <= 50` and `"`" not in r`. If the fleet service returns an empty `stop_reason` for this lane (for example because it only records stop reasons for lanes matching failure patterns), or returns some unrelated safe placeholder, the test still passes. Thus a regression where stop reasons are not recorded or not cut from the provided `session.ended` summary would not be caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_fleet_registry.py:test_stop_reason_is_cut_and_made_safe

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` can never clear a previously recorded stop reason. A successful `lease.released` note (`completed`, `done`, `merged`) is converted to empty text, and the guard `if who and text.strip()` skips updating `out`, so an earlier failure reason remains the agent’s “newest” reason. For example, given events `lease.expired` with `holder=alice`, `reason="HTTP 429"`, then later `lease.released` with `holder=alice`, `note="completed"`, and the lane ledger puts `alice` in `S.STOPPED_DONE`, `registry` preserves reasons for `DONE` lanes and returns `stop_reason="HTTP 429"` for a completed agent instead of no current stop reason (or a clean completion reason).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:70

chunk_findings.detail: `resume`’s “already taken over” guard only rejects a live lease held by another agent, so it can report `eligible: True` while the item is still held by the same agent’s live lease. Given `Entry(name="alice", lane_state=S.STOPPED, item="i")`, and `st.items["i"]` non-terminal with `lease.holder="alice"` and `lease.live(now, grace_s) == True`, the condition `ls.holder != e.name` is false, the stopped-state check passes, and the item is not terminal, so `resume` returns `eligible: True` and a resume command despite the item not being unheld as the docstring requires.

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` treats a later normal `lease.released` (`completed`, `done`, `merged`) as “no stop reason” by setting `text = ""`, but then the `if who and text.strip() and ...` guard prevents that event from updating the agent’s record at all. A previous stop reason therefore survives the newer normal release and can still classify the lane. For example, with `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`, a lane `a` whose ledger state is `S.UNFINISHED` (item unfinished, lease released, item not terminal), and events `lease.expired holder=a reason="HTTP 429" ts=...:10Z` followed by `lease.released holder=a note="completed" ts=...:20Z`, `_signals` still returns the `...:10Z` reason `"HTTP 429"`. `registry` then lists the lane as `failed` with stop reason `"HTTP 429"`, even though the newest stop event was a completed release.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:_signals

chunk_findings.detail: The target-contract contradiction from previous finding 2 is still present. The new docs still tell the user to run `ddflow lanes brief <agent>`, while the declared second positional in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lanes.py` says `with brief or resume: the lane name, or a unique part of it`, and the call only forwards that positional as `lane=a.get("lane")`. If agent names and lane names are not identical, a user following the docs runs `ddflow lanes brief worker-1` with an agent identity, but the surface/API treats `worker-1` as a lane name; a user following the parameter help runs `ddflow lanes brief feature-x` with a lane name, but the docs describe the brief target as an agent. The added parenthetical “a lane is an agent identity” does not remove the contradiction because the same doc line mixes `<lane>` for `resume` with `<agent>` for `brief`, and the CLI `view` help still says `resume <agent>` while the `lane` help says lane name.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/fleet-registry.md:10

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` still cannot clear an older stop reason when the lane ledger still classifies the lane as stopped-unfinished. The new `registry` clearing only applies when `ln.state not in _STOPPED`, so if `LN.build` returns a lane in `S.UNFINISHED` after a later successful `lease.released`, the old reason remains. For example, with lane `alice` in a stopped-unfinished state for item `i`, events `lease.expired` at `ts="1"` with `holder=alice`, `reason="HTTP 429"`, then `lease.released` at `ts="2"` with `holder=alice`, `note="completed"`, and a failure pattern matching `HTTP 429`, `_signals` returns `("1", "HTTP 429")` because the successful release is converted to empty text and the guard skips updating `out`. `registry` keeps that reason and `_class` returns `FAILED`, even though the newest stop event in the log was a successful release.
